name: Machine crunch
cue: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis while your hips stay still.
research: Pin-loaded seated ab crunch machine. Seated, sit bones on the seat (ischia pin), thighs on the seat, knees 90, the feet on a platform hooked under the ankle roller, the upper chest against a roller pad on the pad frame, hands on its handles in front of the shoulders with the upper arms hanging by the ribs (elbows off the abs). The rep is a spinal curl, ribs toward the pelvis, never a hip hinge: the upper thoracic spine leads (via key M), then the lumbar spine, and at the end the pelvis tilts back 8 deg, so the hip angle OPENS (hip flexion 90 -> 82) while the trunk curls (spinal flexion -6 -> 52: lumbar -3 -> 22, thoracic -3 -> 30; thorax tilt -6 -> 44; hip-to-C7 chord -9.5 -> 21.6); the return reverses the order (via key N). Sources: ExRx (lever seated crunch: target rectus abdominis, synergists the obliques; flex the waist, not the hips); Jeff Nippard (loaded crunches done as a spinal curl, the lower back allowed to round, the hips still); the cable crunch's research ranges (spinal flexion -10 -> 60) for the same movement. Machine: the pad frame rides on the chest (the chest roller and the handles move with the thorax), its lever arm runs from a hub beside the hips to the frame's side socket; the hub sits on the spine's curl axis, the centre of the circle through the socket's path at the stretch, mid-curl and peak (beside the lumbar spine at hip level + 0.13 H), so the arm stays rigid (length constant to 1 mm over the loop) and turns 57 deg. A cam on the hub winds the cable back to a guided stack behind the seat; the stack rises 9 cm. A back pad supports the upper back at the stretch. Primary: rectus abdominis; secondary: external obliques. Geometry: tools/design/machine_crunch.mjs.

targets.note: spinal_flexion (thorax tilt minus pelvis tilt) is the crunch itself; hip_flexion opens slightly (the pelvis tucks, never a hinge); trunk_flexion here is the thorax tilt.

camera.note: Research view: the right profile at belly height (az 90, el 0), square to the sagittal plane of the curl. The abs face forward and then down as the trunk curls, so the view turns 28 deg toward the front and drops 8 deg below the belly (az 62, el -8: 29.1 deg in all): the rectus reads as a band from the ribs to the pelvis at the stretch and still under the curled ribs at the peak, the near external oblique (amber) beside it. The lever is on the far side only, behind the trunk from this view, and the pad frame crosses at the upper chest, so nothing of the machine covers the belly; the near upper arm hangs by the ribs behind the oblique.

skinChecks.note: chest roller stays on the upper chest
